name: Associated Press: AP's own page on artificial intelligence in news
title: Associated Press: AP's own page on artificial intelligence in news
answer: The Associated Press publishes this overview of how it uses artificial intelligence in news production. It describes deployed tools for video shotlisting, data analysis, content discovery and photo and video search, plus collaborations with AppliedXL, ShortTok and Merlin. The most useful point is that AP says generated shotlist descriptions are reviewed and edited by editorial staff before publication, and that shotlists are for customer discovery rather than republication. The page also lists AP's AI training, Stylebook guidance and research reports on newsroom readiness and generative AI ethics.

sections.body: The Associated Press publishes this page as an overview of its own artificial intelligence work in news. It is not a research paper or a vendor product page, but a first party account of AP's stated AI use cases, collaborations, training and reports. Its scope covers news gathering, production and distribution, with references to work in 2022, 2023 and 2024. The text does not state a publication date for the page itself.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: AP says it is exploring artificial intelligence to streamline news production and enhance editorial efficiency. AP uses AI tools to analyze video and create shotlists. All generated descriptions are reviewed by editorial staff and edited as needed before publication. Shotlists help customers find shots within a video clip and are not intended to be republished. AP collaborates with AppliedXL to analyze federal registry data and provide actionable news tips to local newsrooms. ShortTok and AP are working together on AI powered content discovery and video curation. Merlin is an AI powered search that recognizes elements within photos and videos and does not rely on descriptions or metadata. AP developed five AI projects in 2023 as part of its Local News AI initiative, funded by the John S. and James L. Knight Foundation. AP says it is committed to equipping journalists with knowledge and skills to navigate AI's role in newsrooms. Through a grant from the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation, its training program offers resources. AP's new artificial intelligence chapter of the AP Stylebook gives guidance on covering AI across every beat and key AI terms. The chapter also forms the basis of a grant funded nationwide training program for AI literacy in journalism. AP's 2022 report on AI in local news examines challenges smaller outlets face when integrating AI. AP's 2024 report on generative AI in journalism looks at how news organizations globally incorporate AI tools into reporting and production, and addresses ethics, evolving newsroom roles, human oversight and training.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that AP developed five AI projects in 2023 as part of its Local News AI initiative, funded by the John S. and James L. Knight Foundation. It names AppliedXL, ShortTok and Merlin as collaborators or tools. It says Merlin is an AI powered search that recognizes elements within photos and videos and does not rely on descriptions or metadata. It says shotlist descriptions are reviewed and edited by editorial staff before publication and that shotlists are not intended to be republished. It cites AP's 2022 report on AI in local news and AP's 2024 report on generative AI in journalism. It says the 2022 series won national awards and led to government action, including a U.S. Justice Department civil rights investigation of a prominent algorithm used in child welfare and state level policy changes. It mentions a grant from the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation for training and a new AP Stylebook artificial intelligence chapter.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in Media can use this page as AP's own account of its AI work in news production. It shows where AP says AI is used, including video shotlisting, data analysis, content discovery and search, and it describes an editorial review step for generated shotlist descriptions. It also points to AP's training, Stylebook guidance and research reports, which can help media readers understand newsroom readiness, ethics and human oversight. The page is useful for comparing AP's stated practice with other news organizations' AI adoption.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Media

sections.body: This is an overview page from AP about its own work, so it is self-reported and promotional in nature. It does not give performance metrics, error rates, costs or independent evaluation. It does not state a publication date for the page itself, though it references work from 2022, 2023 and 2024. The supplied text leaves the training program sentence incomplete. It does not cover other media companies in detail, beyond mentions of local newsrooms and global news organizations in AP's reports. It is not a technical specification or a full case study.
